Bo walks the streets with wonder, the towering buildings reaching higher than the trees back home. His faded and worn clothes are well weathered. As he lightly walks down the streets, the banjo he plays echoes through the crowd. A few odd looks here and there are directed towards him, towards his simple look. A look not seen in the city too often, his straw hat in desperate need of repairs. He hasn't a care in the world... He is here to play. Coming to the big city to seek out musical fame. To hear stories of great adventures. And to possibly carve out an adventure of his own. A group of onlookers nearby giggle at him, his appearance more comical than he anticipated. Tipping his hat towards the small group, he smiles. "Howdy! The name's Cap'n Bo Harkness." He winks and smiles.

You may have noticed this guy hanging out by the ports. But likely not due to his relative shortness, or light tan, or the overalls with makeshift pockets sewn onto them, possibly not even that some started calling him the "night *shifter*" after his working hours - the first thing you might notice could very well be the odd buzzing sound that seems to accompany him every now and then.

If you stop by to talk with him between repairs and other work, you might hear about his hometown in central Europe, where people live in symbiosis with insects that help them in various ways. You might get half-jokingly recruited to join the swarm's new branch in Arcania, which he was sent here to establish a foothold for, but don't worry about it - typically the more details one hears, the more they tend to want to end the topic, so you wouldn't be the only one to pass on the offer. You might also hear something about his work as a mechanic, if you manage to steer the conversation somewhere you don't hear the word "swarm" more often in a sentence than you did the entire last year.
But, if you're curious enough, you could learn more about the teamwork of millions of tiny critters and one carrying them around from Roy the night shifter. As long as you let him finish his repairs.

Blazing Bess
Firearm, two-handed
Rare:  17, 000
When tasked by the general to design a new firearm, the artificer took his meaning all too literally and thus the Blazing Bess was born. A canister of alchemist’s fire has been retrofitted to the barrel of the gun and set up to shoot more “hot” than lead. The canister has 6 charges and requires help from an artificer to refuel over a short rest. Above the trigger there is a switch that can alternate the firing modes, Heat Wave and Scorcher. Changing the mode requires bonus action.

As an action you can spend one of the charges in the following ways.

Heat Wave: A short range blast of flames sears nearby enemies. Each creature in a 15-foot cone must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 2d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. 

Scorcher: A long blast of flames shoots out 30 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 2d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Very Rare: 10, 000

Spin Up

Lightning Shackles 
Bolts of lightning spray from the barrels as you pull the trigger on the spun up gun. You choose up to 5 targets that are all within at least 15 feet of one of the other targets. They must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 4d8 Lightning damage and are restrained as the electric current surges through their body’s, or half as much and suffer no other ill effects on a success.

Static Burst
As a reaction to getting hit by an attack and as long as the chaingun is spun up, you can make all creatures within 5ft of you make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. Taking 2d8 lightning damage and disadvantage on the next attack they make on a failure or half as much and no disadvantage on a success. After using this you need to Spin Up again.

You may as an action, on your next turn, redirect the spell at another target per the spell’s rules. Bows and Crossbows strung with the thread count as a spell focus and deal additional force damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

Staaten Steel (The city)- Weapons forged w/ this material are considered one weight less than normal weapons. Heavy weapons lose the Heavy Property, Non Light weapons gain the light property. Armor forged from this steel are lighter weight, removing any penalty to stealth checks and Heavy armors count as Medium armor and Medium armor count as Light armor

Banshee’s Wail
Firearm (Musket)
7,000 gp
Again the general approached the artificer, demanding a rifle that could strike fear into an enemy whilst they stayed safely in the shadows. Enlisting the help of a Gnermish Gnecromancer, the artificer crafted a most frightening firearm. With a long black finished barrel and silver banding adorned each adorned with protective runes, the Banshee’s Wail was a sight to behold and a terror to hear. 

This musket has an increased short and long range of 300/900, respectively. When you fire the gun an anguished wailing fills the air, each creature in a 15-foot-radius centered on the target creature must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or drop whatever they are holding and become frightened for 1 minute. If a creature succeeds on the saving throw they are immune to the effect for 24 hours.

If you hit a target affected by the frightened condition with Banshee's Wail, you deal an additional 1d12 Necrotic damage.

**Edward 'Ed' Harkness**

**Physical description**
From behind a barrel, in the dark... two bright blue eyes can be seen before the small round face of a young jackalope is seen. Once they are sure that no one has followed them to this place and all trouble is over, they gets up and casually brushes the dust off their light blue coat clashing with their light brown fur. 
When you see them clearly, you can also tell that they're a rather rotund and friendly jackalope. Their expressions often shift from mischievous to dramatic, and can at times be over the top because of their desire to some day be a known actor in a mayor play. 

**Backstory**
After hiding in a ship and being found as a stowaway on the Kilvacan pirate ship, they learned the much needed skills every pirate needs: cleaning and dealing with large pieces of fabric. Eight years later and six months before our adventure begins in Empire City, Ed's ship was detained and ransacked by the Redcoats. They, together with few others, managed to escape imprisonment due to the doubtful origin of the items found in the vessel. After some time of doing odd jobs while looking for their fellow sailors, they were hired to sweep floors by a theater. And it was there that Ed found their inspiration for acting and dancing accompanied by their trusty pan flute. Many, many, many rejections later, they can still be found sweeping floors and helping backstage at the same run-down theater.
